forces: Following the package split in #86 and #87, Core and sdk-node have distinct platform coupling postures that must be independently enforced by package-specific scope gates.
Core must enforce complete platform neutrality with zero host globals and zero host built-in specifiers in authored code and shipped runtime artifacts.

sdk-node must permit only approved Node capabilities (node:async_hooks, node:buffer, node:crypto, node:timers) and first-party SDK Core, while strictly rejecting unapproved built-ins, host globals, and third-party dependencies.
Cross-package placement mutations must prove that moving Node binding code into Core fails closed, and moving transport, browser, or collector code into either SDK package fails closed.

security_justification.audit_integrity: Preserves canonical audit event contracts and structural validation without altering any event metadata or schema constraints.
security_justification.authentication_or_authorization: Does not alter authentication, credential reference validation, or authorization brand registries.
security_justification.authority_provenance: Strengthens package boundaries so authority brands and SPI abstractions remain strictly segregated from platform bindings.
security_justification.concurrency: Validates that ambient context providers remain isolated across async scopes and introduces no concurrent state leaks.
security_justification.confidentiality: Scope gates inspect AST identifiers and specifiers statically, emitting bounded diagnostics without disclosing file contents.
security_justification.cryptography: Verifies that sdk-node uses only approved crypto capabilities (node:crypto randomUUID) and Core uses abstract providers.
security_justification.error_disclosure: Diagnostic emitters bound output length and sanitize control characters, preventing information disclosure on error.
security_justification.external_security_integration: Strictly forbids external transport, collector, exporter, and SIEM integration surfaces in both SDK packages.
security_justification.fail_posture: Unknown coupling, unapproved specifiers, undeclared globals, unreadable files, and empty inventories fail closed.
security_justification.lifecycle: Scope verification runs deterministically during package validation, CI pipelines, and governance gate executions.
security_justification.mutation_ownership: Modifications are strictly confined to declared owned paths in Core, sdk-node, and OpenSpec artifacts.
security_justification.privacy_transformation: Does not process user payloads or personal data; scope verification operates strictly on static source code.
security_justification.resource_retention: Scope checking tools and mutation test suites clean up temporary isolated directories and dispose of resources.
security_justification.retry_or_redelivery: Static verification scripts execute deterministically with idempotent validation results and no retry side-effects.
security_justification.trust_boundary: Enforces explicit trust boundaries between platform-neutral Core, Node platform binding, and forbidden external layers.
